summary.text: Angel Dolejsí is the Greens candidate for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian election. He works as a national operations manager, with experience in the fashion and eyecare industries according to the ABC, which adds that he has been an actor and choreographer. On his party page he argues that corporate interests hold too much sway and that he can represent local renters, families and small businesses free of that influence.

prior_roles.role: Actor and choreographer
prior_roles.note: The ABC says he has been an actor and choreographer; it does not say whether he still is.

priorities.text: Corporate influence is damaging our democracy
Relief from rising housing costs and insecure work
Better-funded public services

sources.title: Caulfield: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Angel Dolejší, Candidate for Caulfield, Australian Greens Victoria

summary.text: David Southwick is the Liberal member for Caulfield, which he has held in the Legislative Assembly since 2010. He was deputy leader of the Victorian Liberals from 2021 to 2024 and took the post again in January 2026. His current shadow portfolios are planning, housing and building, and tourism and major events, and he is recontesting Caulfield in 2026.

occupation.text: Small business owner and university lecturer

summary.text: Geneviève Gilbert is Family First's candidate for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian election. She founded Pink Cross Foundation Australia, a group that says it supports people harmed by the commercial sex industry, and is its executive director. She stood for Family First at the 2025 Prahran by-election, receiving about 1.1 per cent. She holds qualifications in mental health and in visual arts, communication and multimedia.

occupation.text: Founder and executive director, Pink Cross Foundation Australia

prior_roles.role: Founder and executive director

priorities.text: Cost-of-living relief and support for families
Protecting faith-based schools
A legal definition of a woman based on biology

summary.text: Malak Ababneh is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian election. She is studying history at Monash University, has a background in health care, and says she has spent her whole life in Melbourne's south-east. Her party page says she has helped organise protests against the far right and One Nation, and has campaigned on climate, refugee rights, women's rights and Palestine.

priorities.text: I'll fight for you and for a society free from poverty, war and oppression.
Redirecting wealth into fully funded hospitals, schools and community services
More public housing and fair wages
Opposing One Nation and the far right

sources.title: Caulfield: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Michael Abelman is One Nation's candidate for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian election. A community pharmacist, he has run three pharmacies of his own and an import and wholesale business, according to the ABC. He has stood four times before for the Liberal Democrats and the Libertarians, including in Caulfield in 2022 and in the federal seat of Macnamara in 2025. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

prior_roles.role: Owner and operator of three pharmacies
Owner and operator of an import and wholesale business

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia lists a Michael Abelman as the Liberal Democrats candidate here (2.1 per cent). The ABC says he stood four times for the Liberal Democrats and Libertarians but names only Macnamara, so this match is by name and party. The party is now the Libertarian Party.
Stood as a Liberal Democrat; the party is now the Libertarian Party.

Wikipedia lists a Michael Abelman as the Liberal Democrats candidate at this deferred 2022 poll (3.6 per cent). The ABC's count of four past runs fits, but no source names this contest, so the match is by name and party. The party is now the Libertarian Party.

summary.text: Mikaela Stafrace is Labor's candidate for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian election. A lawyer and company director, she moved from legal practice into the not-for-profit sector and founded an organisation that helps women into work through TAFE training. The ABC lists her leadership posts as chief executive of Legacy Melbourne and of Kidney Health Australia and deputy chair of CERES.

summary.text: Yaakov Ziv Shroot, who campaigns as Kovi Shroot, is standing as an independent for Caulfield at the 2026 Victorian state election, on the VEC's list of nominations. He is in his final year of secondary school, and says he decided to run while getting ready to vote for the first time, to show people they need not vote only for the big parties. His website says he has lived in the Caulfield district all his life, acts and writes music, and has been on a synagogue's board, in the Diller Teen Fellows program and in youth leadership at Hineni Youth and Welfare Australia.

occupation.text: VCE student; actor, musician and composer

prior_roles.role: Synagogue board member
Diller Teen Fellow
Apprentice youth councillor
